correctness.rationale: The six equations follow by direct triangular multiplication. Odd characteristic: 2ad=2be=2cf=0 reduces diagonal data to (2q−1)^3 states; a disjoint split by opposite endpoint states gives q³[h(h+q−1)²−R0]+h²q⁴+(q⁵−q³)+2(h−1)(q⁴−q³), with h=2q−1 and R0=q²+h−1+(h−1)(2q+h−2). This expands to q³(2q−1)(11q²−15q+5). Characteristic two: h=q² states give q³h(h−1)(h−2+2q)+hq⁵+h²q⁴−hq³, expanding to q⁵(q⁴+3q³−2q²−2q+1). Each case partition is exhaustive. The entire B-variable fiber in the U+W=0 case is proved, including exceptional zero constrained vectors. Six exact-field linear-rank censuses and two independently programmed literal-multiplication censuses match. Finite experiments support but do not replace the proof.

originality.rationale: The full-text 2014 probability paper defines this invariant and gives a general rank-average identity but does not evaluate the T3 matrix ring and classifies only probabilities at least 15/32, whereas the computed values lie below that cutoff. The inspected 2020 triangular-group paper computes commuting probabilities for invertible upper triangular matrices, not zero Jordan-product counts in the full algebra. The 2012 paper accessible by abstract studies bilinear factorization properties of zero products, not exact fiber cardinalities. Public research records on radical-square-zero quiver rings and other 3-by-3 commutators have incompatible hypotheses and targets. Searches using aliases and the exact polynomial found no dominating published formula. This remains provisional historical priority, not a proof of uniqueness.

value.rationale: Anticommuting probability is a named natural finite-ring invariant. T3 is the first full upper-triangular algebra with J²≠0; the cross term from E12E23=E13 is absent in the smaller T2 algebra and in radical-square-zero quiver examples. Exact counts in the first genuinely composed-path case provide a nontrivial low-spectrum reference point not supplied by the high-probability literature. The different asymptotics 22q^−6 in odd characteristic and q^−3 in characteristic two quantify a sharp structural split. The value is the natural complete finite-field census of this first case; no arbitrary numerical slicing or broader unsolved theorem is claimed.
